label: H.R. 9958
title: Head Start Expansion and Improvement Act of 2026

items.snippet: Specifically, the bill expands eligibility for Head Start programs to include families with incomes below 138% of the federal poverty level.
The bill also adds a definition for public assistance under the Head Start Act to include Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF);

items.item: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC)
items.snippet: the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC);
or the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP).

items.item: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
items.snippet: The bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a program to make grants to Head Start agencies (including Early Head Start agencies) to construct or improve facilities.
HHS must also establish and carry out a program to make grants to Head Start agencies for increasing the compensation paid to employees.
The bill also provides student loan forgiveness for certain Head Start and Early Head Start child care workers.
In particular, the Department of Education must cancel the outstanding balance of principal, interest, and fees due on Federal Direct Loans for a…
…by a Head Start or Early Head Start program for three years, and (2) has provided care or instruction to children enrolled in such a program.

lobbying.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.
lobbying.amount_note: Amounts are the income or expenses reported on the whole LD-2 filing, not money spent on this bill.

caption: This shows who the bill names and who lobbied on it. It does not show who gains or loses, and lobbying can be for or against a bill.

H001081.label: Overlap, not proof of influence.
H001081.caption: Money from this member's itemized individual donors (over $200) whose self-reported employer falls in an industry that also has a client lobbying on this bill. Correlation only; not a quid pro quo. Donors give to campaigns for many reasons, and a lobbying client may have opposed the bill.
H001081.note: None of the lobbying clients on this bill matched an industry rule, so there is nothing to compare.
